sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction; SARL governed by the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code tradition with Germanic influences; EU law directly applicable; non-codified commercial practice supplements the Civil Code and Commercial Code)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU), Articles 49 and 63 (freedom of establishment and free movement of capital)
United States–Luxembourg Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1996, as amended by protocol)
Luxembourg–People's Republic of China Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement and Protocol (signed 2019)
Luxembourg–Germany Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement (as amended; primary cross-border trade partner for subscription-box consumer goods)
Belgium–Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaty network (90+ active BITs)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (Articles 710-1 to 710-26 for SARL); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as consolidated and amended (transposing EU Directive (EU) 2015/849, Directive (EU) 2018/843 and Directive (EU) 2018/1673); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs), as amended; CSSF Regulation 12-02 of 14 December 2012 (AML/CFT obligations of professionals), as amended; Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2016/1675 (high-risk third countries); Law of 2 September 2011 (access to commercial professions / business establishment permit); Code de commerce and RCS/LBR registration regime.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted legitimate-interest access for accredited media and civil society per the amended Law of 13 January 2019; no free public access following the Luxembourg Constitutional Court ruling of 12 February 2022 and the CJEU judgments of 22 November 2022)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Statuts) executed by Luxembourg notarial deed (acte notarié de constitution) — mandatory for SARL formation under Article 710-2 of the Law of 10 August 1915
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des notaires du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg), filed electronically with Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) via the eJustice portal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic notarization; Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) for certified true copies used abroad; Consular Legalization for non-Hague counterpart states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified, notarized copies of passport or national identity documents of all proposed gérants (directors) and ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent authority or notary public of the document holder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) OR Consular Legalization for non-Hague states; sworn translation into French/German/Luxembourgish where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing (extrait du registre) of any foreign corporate shareholder, with chain-of-title UBO documentation to piercing level
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry of the shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization, accompanied by a certified sworn translation into French/German/Luxembourgish

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and proof of source of funds covering the EUR 12,000 minimum share capital (attestation de blocage / couvre-fonds), satisfying Law of 12 November 2004 customer due diligence requirements
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Originator bank (Luxembourg or foreign credit institution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized confirmation for foreign banks; Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization required for non-Hague jurisdictions; EU/EER bank references accepted in original form

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), notably Articles 710-1 (SARL constitution), 710-5 (registered office), 710-13 (share capital payment), 710-15 (management), and 710-17 (general meeting).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) filed electronically for registration in the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SARL minimum share capital is EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and paid in cash or in kind. Cash capital must be deposited in a blocked escrow account at a Luxembourg credit institution until the RCS registration certificate is issued; the block is lifted automatically upon registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the incorporators hereby subscribe for all 12,000 registered shares of EUR 1.00 each, representing the full subscribed share capital, and confirm that such capital has been paid in full into the designated blocked escrow account as required by Article 710-13 of the Law of 10 August 1915. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the registered office is established at [address], Luxembourg City, and the manager is authorised to execute the lease and file all required declarations with the Luxembourg Business Registers. RESOLVED FURTHER: That [Gérant] is appointed sole manager (Gérant) with full administrative powers, and [office manager] is appointed as office manager, each appointment effective upon registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company name reservation and registered address confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS via MyGuichet.lu / e-creation portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request through the LBR online portal. Verify that the proposed name is not identical or confusingly similar to existing Luxembourg or protected international names. Confirm that the registered office address will be located in Luxembourg and that the owner or lessor consents to its use as the company's registered seat.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of incorporators (passport or ID card)
Consent of registered office provider or landlord
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or queried, the applicant may submit an alternative name or file a formal objection with the LBR within 15 days; the reservation may be renewed for an additional fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (notaire) exercising public authentication powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Deliver the final draft articles of association to the chosen Luxembourg notary. The notary verifies the legal capacity and identity of all incorporators, confirms the capital subscription and payment modalities, authenticates the deed, and retains the original notarial register. The notary then prepares the legalisation and transmission to the RCS.
required_dossiers: Certified copies of identity documents for all incorporators/managers
Proof of registered office address and consent
Name reservation confirmation issued by LBR
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies formal defects, the articles are redrafted and re-executed before the same notary; no additional state fee applies for a first correction.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital escrow account and deposit of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (bank or PSP authorised under CSSF regulations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked account in the company's formation name at a Luxembourg bank, deposit the full EUR 12,000 minimum capital, and obtain a non-revocable certificate (attestation de blocage) confirming that the funds are blocked until RCS registration. The certificate must be addressed to the notary.
required_dossiers: Formation name and name reservation certificate
Identity documents of signatories to the account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses the account opening, the applicant may apply to another Luxembourg credit institution; the notary may assist in obtaining a substitute certificate or a bank guarantee from a fully licensed institution.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – RCS Registration Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary files the authenticated deed and supporting documents electronically with the LBR. The LBR verifies legal conformity, assigns the RCS identification number, and registers the company. The registration data is subsequently published in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA).
required_dossiers: Statement of non-criminal record for managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or formal notice, the notary or applicant must provide supplementary information or corrected documents within the prescribed deadline (generally 10-15 days); failure to remedy leads to a new filing fee and re-examination.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, social security and business permit registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS), and Ministry of Economy (via MyGuichet.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the RCS certificate, apply online through MyGuichet.lu for the corporate income tax file, register for VAT (with EU intra-community status if applicable), register the employer with the social security centre, and obtain any municipal or sectoral business authorisation. For warehouse-based subscription box operations, apply for a commercial/industrial authorisation if warehouse surface or logistics activities exceed local administrative thresholds.
required_dossiers: Identities and signatures of authorised managers
Lease agreement for warehousing / logistics premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax or permit application is queried, the applicant may submit corrections via MyGuichet.lu or via the competent administration; an informal appeal or request for review may be lodged within one month, and the registration is retroactively effective from the date of the complete filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economy – Directorate General for Industry and Commerce (Direction générale de l'industrie et du commerce)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific industrial operating licence is mandatory for ISIC 4791 subscription box retailing. However, a municipal commercial authorisation (autorisation d'établissement) may be required if warehousing/logistics activities on the premises are subject to Luxembourg establishment regulation; a municipal business permit for storage and light packaging is obtained through MyGuichet.lu.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement – Environmental Protection Agency of Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Registration only for low-impact storage and light packaging activities under Annex II of the Law of 22 June 2022 on environmental impact assessment; no full EIA report is required for subscription-box warehousing and packing operations below applicable thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharged to municipal sewer must comply with municipal GRV standards (COD ≤ 1,000 mg/l, TSS ≤ 600 mg/l, pH 6.5–9.5). Solvent consumption from any cleaning or packaging processes must remain below the 2 t/yr VOC threshold of Directive 1999/13/EC; waste packaging must be handled by an approved collector and documented under the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required from the Service d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) for the warehouse and logistics premises, including a fire alarm system, escape routes, extinguishers, and emergency lighting. Structural load inspection is required under the Ministry of Labour (ITM) building code to verify the floor load capacity for stacked boxes and pallets. A workplace clearance from ITM confirms compliance with minimum occupational safety levels for lighting, ventilation, ergonomics, and safe handling of material loads.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direct taxes: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD), 45 Boulevard Roosevelt, L-2420 Luxembourg; e-filing via MyGuichet.lu and the ACD e-space. Indirect taxes: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), VAT department; e-filing via MyGuichet.lu. Customs: Administration des Douanes et Accises via the eCDF electronic customs declaration filing system. Commercial register: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), RCS Luxembourg.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: execute the notarized deed of incorporation of the SARL and file the registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) through MyGuichet.lu. Step 2: the RCS registration automatically issues the 13-digit national identification number (matricule), which is the statutory corporate TIN used by both the ACD and the AEDT. Step 3: file VAT registration form Formulaire 564 with the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu; the AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format LU + 8 digits. Step 4: register with the Administration des Douanes et Accises to obtain the customs EORI number (format LU + matricule) for export declarations on eCDF. End-to-end statutory procurement typically completes within 2-4 weeks from RCS filing; the SARL may invoice under the matricule pending VAT-number issuance, but any zero-rated invoice should carry the VAT number once attributed.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope. A Luxembourg SARL is a resident, opaque legal entity taxed at entity level on worldwide business income, with treaty relief and the participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains; no pass-through status exists. Combined headline CIT in Luxembourg City: 17% corporate income tax plus 7% employment-fund surcharge (effective 18.19%) plus 6.75% municipal business tax = 24.94% (municipal rates vary up to about 10.50%); net wealth tax of 0.5% applies to net assets exceeding EUR 500,000, subject to the minimum net-wealth-tax rules. Tax_Exempt_Zone: not applicable; the Luxembourg Freeport grants only customs-duty and VAT suspension within a bonded warehouse, not corporate income-tax exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg has no US-style check-the-box regime and no pass-through election for a SARL. Elective mechanisms available: (i) VAT grouping under Article 60 of the VAT Law, allowing the SARL to form a single taxable person with closely connected Luxembourg-established entities; (ii) fiscal unity (integration fiscale) under Article 164bis LIR for CIT and municipal business tax, requiring an uninterrupted 95% direct or indirect holding and prior ACD approval; (iii) election to waive the Article 57 small-business exemption - mandatory where the SARL claims input-VAT recovery or relies on export zero-rating; (iv) application of the participation exemption (effectively elective, subject to the subject-to-tax and minimum-holding conditions); (v) ATAD 1/2 hybrid-mismatch rules constrain any cross-border hybrid structuring, and specific factual analysis is required before relying on hybrid entity or hybrid instrument treatment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL); Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) as banking and AML/CFT supervisor; European Central Bank (ECB) for eurozone monetary policy coordination.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full eurozone capital and current account convertibility. Luxembourg applies Articles 63-66 TFEU, the OECD Capital Movements Liberalisation Code, and the EU Free Movement of Capital framework; there are no licensing requirements or conversion limits for inward or outward capital transfers. Profit remittance by dividend distribution is unrestricted legally but requires adequate distributable reserves, board approval by the shareholders' meeting, and compliance with the SARL's minimum capital maintenance requirement. Dividends paid to foreign shareholders generally incur Luxembourg 15% withholding tax, reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive where the shareholder holds at least 10% of the capital continuously for 12 months, or reduced under an applicable double tax treaty, with the standard treaty rate typically 5% or 0% depending on shareholding. There are no documentary approval hurdles for conversion of EUR to foreign currency, but banks require completion of ECB BOP statistical declarations for transactions above thresholds and adherence to CSSF anti-money-laundering transaction reporting.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Luxembourg imposes no export proceeds surrender statutory timeline and no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters may retain proceeds in any freely convertible currency, maintain foreign-currency accounts without central bank authorization, and use receipts for operational or treasury purposes. The only compliance duties are accurate BOP/BNLI statistical reporting by the banking counterparty and anti-money-laundering record-keeping. Cash movements of EUR 10,000 or more crossing the EU external border must comply with EU Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 and be declared to customs.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Trade Finance Account
Capital Escrow Account and Global Cash Management Account
Operational Account and Trade Documentary Collection Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High viability is present for EU/EEA electronic money institutions and payment institutions holding a PSD2 authorization that is passported into Luxembourg or licensed by the CSSF. These EMIs can provide SEPA-core accounts, virtual IBANs, commercial cards, API-based treasury controls and faster payments, and are suitable for low-value operational collections, Stripe Billing settlements and Authorize.Net card clearing. Viability is reduced for offshore non-EEA digital EMIs: such institutions generally lack a Luxembourg passport, cannot offer a genuine LU IBAN, are unsuitable for equity capital injections, shareholder loans, corporate tax payments, or bank-intermediated documentary trade, and may create sanctions and AML exposure. If an EMI is used, it must demonstrate client-money safeguarding with a tier-1 credit institution, provide full KYB on the SARL and its UBOs, offer EU payment accounts and SEPA rails, and provide audit access to payment ledger data. A legal opinion from a Luxembourg attorney should be obtained before reliance on any non-bank EMI for mandatory regulatory payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Fully remote onboarding is legally permissible in Luxembourg under CSSF virtual identity guidance and eIDAS-compliant qualified electronic signatures; however, tier-1 Luxembourg banks generally require at least one physical interview of the ultimate beneficial owner, the finance director and one authorized signatory before opening a corporate account. In cases involving a fully non-resident SARL or a cross-border recurring subscription business, banks commonly mandate physical attendance at the Luxembourg branch, original notarized corporate documents, a certified copy of the Luxembourg trade register excerpt, a bank reference from the presenting financial institution, and a detailed source-of-funds narrative. A purely video-only opening is possible only where the bank has a pre-existing institutional relationship, the digital identity is eIDAS-based, and the final AML decision is made by the Luxembourg compliance committee. Realistically, the SARL should plan for an in-person interview to avoid an adverse KYB decision.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-jurisdictional ownership and opaque trust/offshore holding structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg RCS excerpt, articles of association, full-chain beneficial ownership chart, Luxembourg UBO registry (RBE) filing, notarized certificates for all indirect shareholders, source-of-wealth records for each direct shareholder, consolidated group chart, tax residence certificates, and a written commercial substance explanation for the subscription-box business model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High recurring cross-border card-not-present revenue from B2C e-commerce
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI-DSS attestation of compliance, merchant acquirer agreements, processed sales ledger, chargeback and refund ratio reports, anti-fraud transaction monitoring policy, CNPD data-protection registration, customer-ticket escalation procedures, and the full payment services agreement with Stripe Billing or Authorize.Net proving settlement directly into the LU SARL bank account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, embargo exposure or high-risk end-customer destinations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU/OFAC/UN sanctions screening policy, IP and device geolocation blocking, denied-party list software output, customer-country export classification by HS code, board resolution prohibiting sales to sanctioned jurisdictions, and forward-looking compliance certification with quarterly independent sanctions testing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder loan or foreign-currency capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized loan agreement or share subscription deed, board minutes approving terms, ECB BOP declaration data, source-of-funds evidence from an EU licensed bank, financial projections demonstrating treasury need, and confirmation that the transaction is not a disguised money laundering structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner designated as a politically exposed person (PEP)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Enhanced due diligence profile, verified source of wealth and source of funds documentation, current professional and business background, previous bank reference, independent external audit letter, legal counsel opinion on the legitimacy of the capital structure, and a commitment to provide risk updates to the Luxembourg AML compliance officer at least semi-annually.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity contributions and shareholder loans should be routed by SEPA Credit Transfer for euro transfers from EEA counterparties, or by SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA remittances. The receiving Luxembourg bank must see the mandated purpose code: 'Direct investment - Equity capital' for share subscription and 'Direct investment - Loans' or 'Other investment - Loans' for shareholder debt. The beneficiary should be the exact legal name 'LU_SARL' with the Luxembourg IBAN. Verification documentation comprises the notarized share subscription deed, updated RCS excerpt, board resolution, bank account confirmation, funding bank statement, UBO declarations, and a capital-payment certificate prepared by a Luxembourg notary or auditor. All receipts above EUR 12,500 are captured in the BCL balance-of-payments and direct investment statistics and may trigger enhanced monitoring where the remitter is located in a non-transparent jurisdiction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements for subscription-box merchandise should use: (i) SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments within SEPA zone; (ii) SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA suppliers; (iii) documentary letters of credit issued under UCP 600 for high-value or first-transaction imports; (iv) documentary collection for established low-risk trade partners; and (v) supply-chain finance instruments if the bank has granted trade credit limits. All disbursements must reconcile to supplier invoices, HS tariff codes, Incoterms, and the approved treasury cash-flow forecast. The bank's BOP reporting system must code payments as 'International Trade in Goods' or 'Trade Settlement' with corresponding invoice and bill-of-lading references. For recurring monthly procurement, the SARL should run consolidated payment batches and automated duplicate-invoice controls to minimize processing friction and ensure audit trail completeness.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on non-fully convertible currencies when supported by physical procurement exposure
FX swaps and rollovers for cash-flow matching of supplier and dividend cycles
Cross-currency interest rate swaps under ISDA/CSA documentation
Structured FX options, including capped forwards and collars, used exclusively for hedging under Luxembourg MiFID II rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory accounts (balance sheet, profit and loss, and notes) filed and published in RESA
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after financial year-end; for a calendar-year SARL by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Two-month formal notice then referral to the Public Prosecutor; judicial injunction; court-ordered strike-off from RCS and a criminal fine of up to EUR 10,000 on managers

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) approving annual accounts, discharge of managers and profit allocation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate body; minutes filed in the statutory minute book and kept at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year-end (30 June for calendar-year SARL); court-authorised extension available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil and criminal liability of directors, nullity of defective shareholder decisions and blockage of RCS filing; a shareholder may petition the court to compel the AGM

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership data in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month following the annual RBE invitation (anniversary-based, usually the same month each year); a replacing declaration is due within 30 days of any beneficial ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines ranging from EUR 125 to EUR 250,000 per case, with broader manager-level sanctions for repeated non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Combined annual tax return covering corporate income tax (IRC), municipal business tax (ICC) and net wealth tax (IFT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 December of the year following the tax year; the ACD may fix a different individual filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of assessed tax; default interest of 0.6% per month; ex-officio assessment if no return is submitted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Recurring value-added tax (TVA) returns plus annual recapitulative statement for intra-community transactions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly or quarterly TVA returns per notified frequency (electronic filing by the 15th of the month following the period); annual recapitulative statement for intra-EU deliveries by 31 January of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of VAT due; monthly interest of 0.8%; automatic tax assessment; criminal liability for intentional non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Minimum net wealth tax settlement and annual IFT computation embedded in the combined tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable with the combined annual tax return (generally by 31 December of year Y+1); annual minimum of EUR 3,210 for a commercial SARL not holding predominately financial assets
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Tax surcharge of 10% and monthly interest of 0.6%; enforced collection and potential seizure of bank accounts after formal demand

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audit and update of statutory registers (members, directors, minutes) and verification against UBO filings
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Held at the registered office; certified by the SARL manager and associated fiduciary agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Audited at each AGM and updated immediately after any share transfer or director change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Inaccurate registers trigger director liability, criminal fines, loss of enforceability of shareholder rights against the company, and adverse findings in lender due diligence

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of an approved statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) for a SARL exceeding at least two of three EU small-enterprise thresholds: balance sheet total over EUR 4.4 million, net turnover over EUR 8.8 million, or average staff of 45; a full large-entity audit is triggered at two of three higher thresholds: EUR 20 million balance sheet, EUR 40 million turnover, or 250 employees
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP deriving from the law of 19 December 2002 and EU Accounting Directives; IFRS as adopted in the EU is voluntary except for listed groups; annual accounts prepared in EUR

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must electronically confirm the RBE data within one month of the register's annual invitation; any change in beneficial ownership requires a replacement declaration within 30 days; the RBE is not publicly accessible, only authorised authorities and obliged entities may inspect it; shareholding transfers do not reset UBO status if the same individuals remain beneficial owners
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of general meetings and management decisions

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,300 - 3,500 (EUR 1,200 - 3,200) for fiduciary registered office, annual agent services and company secretarial support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 for sub-threshold SARL; voluntary small-audit fee range USD 5,400 - 16,200 (EUR 5,000 - 15,000); full statutory audit for larger entities USD 16,200 - 54,000 (EUR 15,000 - 50,000)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City: 17% corporate income tax + 6.75% municipal business tax + 7%-of-CIT employment fund contribution); aggregate rate varies with the commune of the SARL's establishment.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP Box (80% exemption on qualifying IP revenues, effective rate approximate 5%); full participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains (10% holding for 12 months); Notional Interest Deduction on new equity; R&D investment tax credit; reduced rates under newly negotiated DTA tax-sparing provisions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 540 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités); mandatory electronic filing via the MyGuichet.lu portal and the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration eCDF e-filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Fiscal year ended 31 December N: statutory filing deadline 31 May N+1; the Luxembourg administration annually announces an automatic deadline extension to 31 December N+1 for ordinary filings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identifies the taxable period (commercial year opening and closing dates) and the SARL's Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) registration number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporate taxpayers with a Luxembourg permanent establishment must use the non-resident section and attach the foreign head-office tax residency certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of commercial accounting profit under Luxembourg GAAP against taxable profit; subscription-box revenue, cost of goods sold, fulfilment charges and operating expenses flow from the audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only the taxable profit attributable to the Luxembourg PE in accordance with LIR Art. 132 is entered; head-office general costs must be allocated on an arm's-length basis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses to add back: 50% of independent management/supervisory board members' fees, income taxes, undisclosed profit distributions, fines, penalties and excessive directors' remuneration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identical add-backs are required for the Luxembourg PE's tax base to prevent erosion of the municipal business tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exempt or preferentially taxed income: participation-exemption dividends, IP Box qualifying income (80% exempt), Notional Interest Deduction and foreign PE loss deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Exemptions apply only where the underlying asset or activity is effectively connected to the Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Loss carryforward utilisation: admissible prior-year taxable losses are applied against current-year taxable profit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Luxembourg PE losses are ring-fenced and carried forward separately from the foreign head office's results.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Determination of the assessed taxable base before application of tax credits; the basis is the aggregate taxable income for corporate income tax and municipal business tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the PE's separately computed taxable income; municipal business tax applies in the commune where the PE is located.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computation: 17% CIT, 7% employment fund contribution calculated on the CIT amount, and the commune's municipal business tax rate (6.75% in Luxembourg City); applicable tax credits are then deducted.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 7% employment fund surcharge and municipal business tax apply to the Luxembourg PE unless a DTA allocation rule otherwise apportions the tax base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory attachment disclosing material controlled transactions: SaaS/PaaS platform royalties, international logistics payments, intercompany financing and subscription fee flows; the selected arm's-length method is described.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border transactions between the foreign head office and the Luxembourg PE must be documented under the internal cost-allocation and transfer pricing policy.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing of Form 540 triggers: estimation of taxable income under Abgabenordnung § 217; a surcharge of up to 10% on the assessed CIT and municipal business tax for unjustified delay; monthly late-payment interest of 0.6% on unpaid tax; administrative fines of EUR 250 to EUR 1,250 for ordinary defaults, escalated up to EUR 25,000 for gross negligence or repeat violations; the legal representative(s) and directors are jointly exposed to the same fines.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% under LIR Art. 151; reduced to 0% where the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive applies (minimum 10% direct holding for 12 months) or where a DTA reduces the rate for a qualifying corporate shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Relief at source is not automatic. The Luxembourg SARL must pre-verify: (i) the parent's tax-residence certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority, generally not older than six months; (ii) the uninterrupted 10% shareholding for at least 12 months, or a sworn statement of holding intention; (iii) beneficial ownership of the dividends and absence of GAAR/Principal Purpose Test abuse. The verified file is retained for inspection by the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD). If relief at source is refused, the foreign parent must file a refund claim with the ACD within the statutory limitation period, attaching the TRC, the withholding voucher and the legal documentation package.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg imposes no statutory withholding tax on outbound royalties or interest; 0% is confirmed for qualifying EU/EEA group companies under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive; applicable DTA rates generally range from 0% to 10%, with any source tax arising only under the counterparty jurisdiction's domestic law.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File mandatory where the SARL's annual net turnover exceeds EUR 5 million and the group's consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 50 million; Master File mandatory where group consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 750 million; documentation must be contemporaneous and filed with the annual Form 540 annex.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a UAE-style ESR point-scoring regime, but substantive human and physical presence is legally required to access treaty benefits, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, finance branch exemptions, and favourable circulars. The ACD invokes the GAAR (LIR Art. 6 §1), ATAD/ATAD-II provisions (LIR Arts. 56–56bis), and the OECD MLI Principal Purpose Test to deny benefits to letterbox companies lacking premises, staff, local decision-making, and operative bank accounts.
